articles.title: US, South Korea and Japan Reaffirm Commitment to North Korea’s ‘Complete Denuclearization’ - Opinion Nigeria
articles.summary: US, South Korea and Japan Reaffirm Commitment to North Korea’s ‘Complete Denuclearization’  Opinion Nigeria
articles.full_text:
The United States, South Korea and Japan have renewed their commitment to the “complete denuclearization” of North Korea as Pyongyang continues to reject disarmament ahead of possible nuclear talks with Washington.
Speculation has grown over a possible meeting between US President Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during next month’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in China, following repeated overtures by Trump for renewed nuclear negotiations.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun and Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi reaffirmed their position during a meeting on Friday on the sidelines of the Group of 20 (G20) gathering in Atlanta, Georgia.
According to the US State Department, the three officials “reaffirmed their resolute commitment to the complete denuclearization” of North Korea.
They also pledged to ensure the “full implementation” of United Nations Security Council resolutions, including measures prohibiting support for revenue-generating activities linked to North Korea’s nuclear and ballistic missile programmes.
Despite years of international sanctions, North Korea, which enjoys support from Russia and China, has legally entrenched its status as a nuclear-armed state. Its government has repeatedly insisted that its nuclear arsenal is permanent and irreversible.
Trump open to meeting Kim
Trump has repeatedly expressed willingness to engage Pyongyang in nuclear negotiations while reducing joint military exercises with South Korea, a key US ally.
The US president departed from longstanding American policy last year when he acknowledged that North Korea was already “sort of a nuclear power”. He also signalled that he was “100 percent” open to meeting Kim, although the North Korean leader did not respond to the proposal.
Analysts and South Korea’s intelligence agency believe Kim may have communicated Pyongyang’s position on possible talks with Trump to Beijing during a recent visit to the Chinese border city of Dandong.
South Korea’s President Lee Jae Myung, who has adopted a more conciliatory approach towards Pyongyang, has repeatedly called for dialogue without preconditions.
In September, Lee suggested that Washington consider pursuing a freeze on North Korea’s nuclear programme rather than demanding its immediate dismantlement, in exchange for sanctions relief.
However, critics argue that such a proposal could amount to tacit recognition of North Korea as a nuclear-armed state while allowing Pyongyang to secure sanctions relief without surrendering its weapons.
Some analysts also believe China may be moving towards accepting North Korea’s nuclear status, citing the absence of references to denuclearisation in statements issued after Kim met Chinese President Xi Jinping in June.
Meanwhile, Pyongyang on Saturday criticised a joint statement issued by a group of countries monitoring the implementation of sanctions against it.
North Korea insisted that “the stereotyped sanctions racket of the US and the West can neither influence the position of the DPRK (North Korea) as a nuclear weapons state”.

articles.title: US, South Korea, Japan reaffirm commitment to North Korea denuclearization - Türkiye Today
articles.summary: US, South Korea, Japan reaffirm commitment to North Korea denuclearization  Türkiye Today
articles.full_text:
The U.S., South Korea and Japan reaffirmed their “resolute commitment” to the complete denuclearization of North Korea during trilateral talks Friday in Atlanta, while also signing a new agreement to expand cooperation in the Pacific Arctic.
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun and Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting to discuss regional security, economic resilience and energy cooperation.
The ministers reaffirmed their commitment to fully implementing U.N. Security Council resolutions and enforcing sanctions targeting revenue for North Korea’s nuclear and ballistic missile programs.
They also praised the Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team for documenting North Korean sanctions violations and evasion.
The meeting came amid speculation over a possible meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during next month’s APEC summit in China.
Trump has repeatedly expressed openness to renewed nuclear talks with Pyongyang and previously said he was “100 percent” open to meeting Kim.
South Korean President Lee Jae Myung has also offered talks with Pyongyang without preconditions and suggested in September that Washington could pursue a freeze of North Korea’s nuclear program in exchange for sanctions relief.
North Korea, however, has declared its nuclear arsenal permanent and irreversible and has enshrined its status as a nuclear-armed state in law.
Rubio, Cho and Motegi also signed a Memorandum of Cooperation establishing the Trilateral Arctic Pacific Partnership, or TAPP, to explore maritime cooperation and economic partnerships in the Pacific Arctic.
The three countries also expressed opposition to economic coercion and the weaponization of supply chains.
They reviewed progress on a trilateral agreement on Small Modular Reactor deployments signed in Ankara on the sidelines of a NATO summit in July.
The ministers also emphasized peace and stability in the Taiwan Strait, while Rubio raised concerns about China’s actions in the South China Sea, East China Sea and Yellow Sea, as well as Russia-China cooperation that Washington says undermines Indo-Pacific stability.

articles.title: South Korea, U.S., Japan Reaffirm North Korea Denuclearization Commitment - 조선일보
articles.summary: South Korea, U.S., Japan Reaffirm North Korea Denuclearization Commitment  조선일보
articles.full_text:
The foreign ministers of South Korea, the United States, and Japan agreed on October 30 (local time) that North Korea must be completely denuclearized and that peace and stability in the Taiwan Strait must be maintained. They also agreed to cooperate in the Arctic Pacific region.
According to a joint statement from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the U.S. Department of State, and Japan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Minister Cho Hyun, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi held a trilateral meeting for approximately 20 minutes starting at 5:05 p.m. in Atlanta, where the G20 (20 countries) foreign ministers’ meeting was taking place.
The three ministers reaffirmed their firm commitment to the complete denuclearization of North Korea and the full implementation of United Nations Security Council resolutions, including the prohibition of financial support for North Korea’s nuclear and ballistic missile programs. In this regard, they highly evaluated the activities of the Multinational Sanctions Monitoring Team (MSMT), which monitors North Korea’s violations and evasions of Security Council resolutions. The MSMT was newly established by 11 countries, including South Korea, the U.S., and Japan, after the UN expert panel, which had been investigating North Korea’s sanctions violations, was dissolved in 2024 due to Russia’s veto in the Security Council.
The three ministers also agreed to maintain a robust deterrence posture against North Korea through close coordination and to continue solidarity in addressing malicious cyber activities that fund North Korea’s nuclear and ballistic missile programs. They urged North Korea to join efforts to ease tensions on the Korean Peninsula and establish peace.
The ministers exchanged opinions on global issues, including “attempts to unilaterally change the status quo by force or coercion,” and reaffirmed their position that peace and stability in the Taiwan Strait must be maintained and that they oppose “economic coercion and the weaponization of supply chains.” They also agreed to further strengthen cooperation in diversifying critical mineral supply chains and advancing technologies such as small modular reactors (SMRs) and artificial intelligence (AI).
The three ministers signed a “Cooperation Memorandum of Understanding (MOC) for the Trilateral Arctic Pacific Partnership (TAPP).” The agreement aims to deepen cooperation in maritime safety, emergency response, and economic activities in the Arctic Pacific region. The three countries plan to develop specific cooperation measures through a new working group to be established under the Arctic Council.
Each country emphasized different points. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated that Minister Cho Hyun stressed South Korea’s role as a “pacemaker” in establishing a peace regime on the Korean Peninsula and resuming North Korea-U.S. dialogue under close South Korea-U.S. coordination. The U.S. Department of State noted that Secretary Rubio highlighted a “free and open Indo-Pacific,” raising concerns about China’s attempts to strengthen control over the South China Sea, coercive behavior in the East China Sea and Yellow Sea, and Russia-China cooperation undermining peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific region. Japan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs emphasized that the solidarity of Japan, the U.S., and South Korea is essential for regional peace and stability, stressing the need to enhance joint training, cybersecurity cooperation, and supply chain collaboration. Motegi also reaffirmed the support of South Korea and the U.S. for resolving the issue of Japanese citizens abducted by North Korea.
Separately, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced that Minister Cho Hyun held a bilateral meeting with Secretary Rubio, where they exchanged opinions on “all pending issues between South Korea and the U.S., including bilateral relations, high-level exchanges, and visa matters.”

articles.title: US, South Korea and Japan reaffirm commitment to North Korea’s denuclearization — Korea Herald - UA.NEWS
articles.summary: US, South Korea and Japan reaffirm commitment to North Korea’s denuclearization — Korea Herald  UA.NEWS
articles.full_text:
In Atlanta, United States, the foreign ministers of South Korea, the United States and Japan reaffirmed their commitment to pursuing the complete denuclearization of North Korea and the implementation of UN Security Council resolutions. The meeting of Cho Hyun, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi took place on the sidelines of the G20 meeting, Korea Herald reports.
Statements on North Korea
According to the US State Department, the ministers reaffirmed their firm commitment to the complete denuclearization of North Korea and the full implementation of UN Security Council resolutions. This includes measures prohibiting activities that generate revenue for Pyongyang’s nuclear and ballistic missile programs.
The parties also noted the work of the Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team, which tracks and reports violations and attempts to evade UN sanctions against North Korea. Cho Hyun said that South Korea would continue to facilitate the resumption of dialogue between Washington and Pyongyang and the establishment of a lasting peace regime on the Korean Peninsula, coordinating its actions with the United States.
In addition, the diplomats stressed the importance of preserving peace and stability in the Taiwan Strait.
More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram.
Economic and maritime cooperation
Marco Rubio expressed concern over China’s actions in the South China Sea, East China Sea and Yellow Sea, as well as cooperation between China and Russia, which, he said, threatens peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific region.
The ministers expressed shared concern over the vulnerability of global supply chains amid international uncertainty and the energy crisis. They agreed to deepen cooperation to diversify supply chains for critical minerals, develop small modular reactors, artificial intelligence and other critical and emerging technologies.
Arctic-Pacific Partnership
South Korea, the United States and Japan also signed a memorandum of cooperation to establish the Trilateral Arctic-Pacific Partnership. It is intended to expand maritime and economic cooperation in the Pacific Arctic region.
